chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Aasim ibn Humayd, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the teeth and the arms which are broken deliberately; is there a compensation (arsh) for them or retaliation (qawd)? He said: Retaliation. I said: So if they double the wergild? He said: If they please him with whatever he desires, then it is for him.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling for deliberately breaking teeth or arms, and can compensation replace retaliation?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that deliberate fractures of the teeth and arm incur qawd (retaliation) rather than fixed diyah, reflecting the Shia juristic view that these injuries are treated with the flexibility of retaliation. It further establishes the victim's autonomy to accept any agreed-upon compensation, even if it exceeds the standard wergild, highlighting the consensual nature of blood money settlements in Shia fiqh.
